what_its_for: Mavacamten is used to treat a heart condition called obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). This is a condition where the heart muscle becomes too thick, making it harder for your heart to pump blood properly. This medicine helps relax the heart muscle so your heart can pump blood more easily, which can help reduce symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, and feeling faint or dizzy during activity.
how_to_take: Take mavacamten by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsule whole — do not open, crush, or chew it. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Do not change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly could make your condition worse.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose (usually 2.5 mg or 5 mg once daily) and may slowly adjust your dose over time based on how your heart is responding. Your doctor will use a special heart ultrasound test called an echocardiogram to check how your heart is working and decide if your dose needs to be changed. Never take more or less than your prescribed dose without your doctor's approval.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 12 hours since your scheduled time, take it as soon as you remember. If it has been more than 12 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store mavacamten at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in a cool, dry place. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine properly — ask your pharmacist how to safely throw it away.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your body and raise the risk of side effects. Do not drink alcohol heavily, as this can worsen heart function. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, and herbal supplements. Many common medicines — including certain antifungals, antibiotics, seizure medicines, antidepressants, and heartburn medicines — can interact with mavacamten and change how well it works or increase side effects. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should know that this medicine can harm an unborn baby — use reliable birth control and talk to your doctor right away if you become pregnant.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: sudden worsening of shortness of breath, new or worsening swelling in your legs or ankles, rapid weight gain (more than 2-3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week), feeling faint or actually fainting, a very fast or irregular heartbeat, unusual tiredness or weakness, or chest pain. Also contact your doctor if you start any new medications or supplements, since drug interactions are a serious concern with this medicine. Your doctor will need to monitor your heart with regular echocardiograms and possibly blood tests to make sure the medicine is working safely.
when_it_works: Mavacamten starts working soon after you begin taking it, but it may take several weeks to months before you notice a meaningful improvement in your symptoms. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular heart ultrasounds (echocardiograms) — typically at 4, 8, and 12 weeks after starting or changing your dose. Do not be discouraged if you do not feel better right away. It is important to keep taking your medicine as directed even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Mavacamten can cause serious harm to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant must use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted. Older adults: Older patients can take this medicine but should be monitored closely for side effects. Children: This medicine is not currently approved for use in children. CYP2C19 poor metabolizers: Some people naturally process this drug more slowly due to their genetics. Your doctor may check this with a genetic test and adjust your dose if needed.
